description.value:
Compatibility: Bestial

Zhier are quadrupedal, extremely long living, sapient beasts somewhere between a wolf and a large feline. They typically have short fur, long, tuft-tipped tails, agile bodies, and tough manes either around the neck or spine. Their fur color stretches from more naturalistic oranges and whites, to striking blues and greens, and is often accented by certain amounts of dyed fur. Their manes range from full-neck manes like a lion, to tracing the spine like a hyena, and in either instance, the manes can be soft and silky or rough or scraggled. Their wolf-like eyes on the other hand, are fully genetic, with yellow or gold, orange, hazel, light brown, light green, amber, and blue being most common.

As one of the few fully intelligent quadrupeds, Zhier often have a difficult time fitting into bipedal societies, but their resilience and mental flexibility makes adaptation easier than one might think. Despite their lack of hands, zhier mouths are incredibly well evolved to hold, manipulate, and wield objects. Zhier have impressively strong neck and jaw muscles that allow them to quickly pick up and wield weapons that most would struggle to use with one hand. In fact, many zhier prefer gripping a weapon in their teeth over biting and tearing that might chip their valuable teeth. Weapons can be sharpened and repaired, and bring versatility and range to the table that teeth alone cannot. The more hominid races are often bewildered by a zhier’s intelligence, mistaking them for talking lions, wolves, tigers, etc. As versatile as they can be, zhier are considered an anomaly in the animal kingdom, and so outside influences, whether deities or strange magics have been suspected. Though asking a zhier will lead to the conclusion that it’s their connection to nature that defines their shape, not the other way around.

To this point, all zhier are born with a deep, personal connection to an element of nature that is said to permeate them to their very core. This connection is both physical and spiritual, manifesting most obviously in a zhier’s corresponding fur color. This element is most highly attuned, however, to the tip of their tail, which radiates with their element. In a pinch, zhier can swing their tail at creatures like a flail that bursts with elemental energy to injure their target.
A zhier’s control over their spirit element grows with them over time, and the nurturing of this gift can be considered a spiritual experience in its own right; an act of self-improvement. Surprisingly, these elements are not genetic—Zhier of one element can give birth to a zhier of any other. Some say that the element is based on a zhier’s personality, or that the personality is based on the element. Others relate it to seasons or weather or even energies in the air. No matter the case, the elemental attunement has a great effect on a zhier’s life, determining what capabilities and roles it can undertake. Zhier mythology considers these elements a gift of nature, a call to action unique to each zhier. This can be taken further with the introduction of their sign.

Core Zhier Traits

  • Attribute Increase: Your Dexterity and Wisdom both increase by 1.
  • Lifespan: Zhier live tremendously long lives, with some being known to live into the low thousands. Zhier reach a physical maturity sometime in their 30s-40s. However, their extended lifespan gives them a different perspective on mental maturity, with most zhier being considered adults between their 70s-90s.
  • Size: Medium; Zhier are typically around 4 to 5 feet long and 2-2.5 feet high while on all fours, and can weigh between 120 to 200 lbs.
  • Speed: Your base ground speed is 30 feet.
  • Languages: You can speak, read, and write Common and Landspeak.
  • Skill Proficiency: You have proficiency in the Wisdom (Instinct) skill.
